units.title: Stocks and Thickeners
units.blurb: The foundation of the French kitchen, and how sauces get their body.

units.title: The Sauces
units.blurb: The five mother sauces, their children, emulsions and pan sauces.

topics.title: Stocks: White, Brown, Fish and Vegetable
topics.short: Bones or vegetables, aromatic mirepoix and cold water, simmered (never boiled) and skimmed: chicken about 3 to 4 hours, beef or veal 6 to 8, fish 30 to 45 minutes.
topics.trouble: Cooks boil stock hard, which clouds it with fat and particles.

topics.title: Roux, Slurries and Liaisons
topics.short: Roux is equal weights of fat and flour cooked to white, blond or brown; slurries are starch stirred into cold liquid; a liaison of yolks and cream enriches at the end.
topics.trouble: Cooks add cold roux to cold liquid and get lumps, or boil a liaison and scramble the yolks.

topics.title: The Five Mother Sauces
topics.short: Escoffier's leading sauces: béchamel (milk and roux), velouté (white stock and roux), espagnole (brown stock and brown roux), tomato and hollandaise.
topics.trouble: Learners memorize five names without the pattern: each mother is a liquid plus a way to thicken it.

topics.title: Small Sauces: Children of the Mothers
topics.short: Add cheese to béchamel for Mornay, mushrooms and cream to velouté for suprême, shallots and wine to demi-glace for bordelaise, tarragon reduction to hollandaise for béarnaise.
topics.trouble: Learners mix up which mother a small sauce comes from; ask what liquid is in it.

topics.title: Emulsions: Mayonnaise, Hollandaise, Vinaigrette, Beurre Blanc
topics.short: Tiny drops of fat held in water with help from an emulsifier such as egg yolk or mustard; add the fat slowly, and keep warm emulsions warm, not hot.
topics.trouble: Cooks pour the oil in too fast or let hollandaise get too hot, and the sauce breaks.

topics.title: Reductions and Pan Sauces
topics.short: Deglaze the browned bits (fond) with wine or stock, reduce, and finish with cold butter swirled in off the heat (monter au beurre).
topics.trouble: Cooks reduce with salt already in, so the sauce ends too salty; season at the end.

topics.title: Clear, Cream and Purée Soups
topics.short: Broths and consommé are clear; cream soups are thickened; purées are thickened by the vegetables or beans themselves; bisques are shellfish soups.
topics.trouble: Cooks blend hot soup in a sealed blender full to the top; steam can force the lid off.
